skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, QA checklists, sample URLs, and timestamp generation. One real issue remains: both helper scripts use eval with interactive user input, which can enable command injection when the scripts are run. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts use eval with interactive user input.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval assignments with safe Bash indirect assignment, such as printf -v, or use explicit case statements for allowed variables.

remediation.issue: Optional shell helpers increase execution risk for a documentation-focused skill.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer Markdown templates or a safer script implementation, and document that scripts are optional and should be reviewed before running.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell eval on User Input
semantic_findings.description: Both interactive helper scripts assign user input through eval inside prompt_input. A crafted response can break out of the assignment and execute shell commands when the script runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts read interactive input and interpolate it into eval-based assignments. The variable names are fixed, but the user-controlled value can still alter the evaluated shell text.

content.user_title: Plan QA Tests and Bug Reports
content.value_statement: QA teams need consistent test plans, cases, regression suites, and bug reports. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce structured QA deliverables.
actual_capabilities: Creates test plans with scope, objectives, risks, entry criteria, and exit criteria.
Generates manual test cases with preconditions, steps, expected results, and test data.
Builds smoke, targeted, and full regression suite outlines with priorities and pass criteria.
Produces structured bug report templates with environment details, impact, evidence, and reproduction steps.
Provides Figma validation checklists for layout, spacing, typography, color, and component states.
Includes optional interactive shell scripts for creating Markdown test cases and bug reports.
limitations: It does not execute tests or verify application behavior automatically.
Figma validation depends on user-provided design access and available MCP context.
Generated QA artifacts need human review before release decisions.
The included shell scripts should be reviewed before use because they handle local user input.

use_cases.title: Create Release Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Build a test plan and regression outline for a new feature or release candidate.

use_cases.title: Turn Requirements Into Test Cases
use_cases.description: Convert product requirements into prioritized manual test cases with clear expected results.

use_cases.title: Validate UI Against Design
use_cases.description: Prepare Figma comparison checklists for spacing, typography, colors, responsive layout, and states.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a QA test plan for the user authentication feature. Include scope, risks, environments, entry criteria, and exit criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Manual Cases
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for hands-on QA execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate six manual test cases for the checkout flow. Include priority, preconditions, steps, expected results, and test data.

prompt_templates.title: Build Regression Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a regression suite for the payment module. Separate smoke, critical path, and full regression tests with execution order and pass criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Design and Bug Reporting
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow across UI validation and defect documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the login page against the provided Figma design context. List visual discrepancies and create a bug report for the highest impact issue.

output_examples.output: A prioritized set of checkout test cases covering valid payment, invalid card handling, empty cart behavior, promo codes, and guest checkout.

output_examples.input: Create a regression suite for payments.
output_examples.output: A regression outline with smoke tests first, critical payment paths next, lower priority edge cases last, and clear pass criteria.
A bug report with title, severity, priority, environment, reproduction steps, expected result, actual result, impact, and evidence checklist.

best_practices: Provide requirements, target platforms, test data needs, and release context before asking for QA artifacts.
Review generated cases with developers, designers, and product owners before execution.
Keep regression suites focused on critical paths and update them after each release.
anti_patterns: Do not accept vague test steps without expected results.
Do not use generated bug reports without verifying reproduction steps and environment details.
Do not run optional shell scripts before reviewing their local behavior.

faq.question: Can this skill execute tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It plans tests and creates documentation, but a tester or automation system must execute them.

faq.question: Does it support Figma validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides design comparison checklists when you supply Figma context or MCP access.

faq.question: What artifacts can it create?
faq.answer: It can create test plans, manual test cases, regression suite outlines, Figma validation checklists, and bug reports.

faq.question: Is it only for QA engineers?
faq.answer: No. Product managers, designers, developers, and release managers can use it to structure testing work.

faq.question: Are the shell scripts required?
faq.answer: No. They are optional helpers for local Markdown generation and should be reviewed before use.

faq.question: Can it replace human QA review?
faq.answer: No. It improves structure and coverage, but humans must validate accuracy, priority, and release impact.
